mainTopic: Is later-acquired property (דאיקני) liened? Proofs are pushed off as following רבי מאיר. Then: when two lenders both lien future property, the הלכה is that they split it.
overview: The גמרא asks whether a lien takes hold of property the borrower buys after the loan (דאיקני), even once he sells it or leaves it to his heirs. Two proofs are brought, one from the משנה about postdated שטרות and one from a ברייתא about a creditor taking a field that the buyer improved. Each proof is pushed off with the same answer: the source follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a person can transfer something not yet in existence. The גמרא then asks a follow-up question that only comes up if דאיקני is liened. If someone borrowed from two lenders and only afterward acquired property, which lender has the lien? A ruling from ארץ ישראל says the first lender acquires, but רב הונא and רבה בר אבוה say they split it. רב אשי changed his mind and ended with 'they split it,' and that is the הלכה. The improved-field ברייתא is then used to challenge this ruling. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's word 'collects' means half the improvement.

steps.title: The earlier proof is pushed off: that משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects a proof brought just before this point by saying that the source follows רבי מאיר's individual view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, whose view is this משנה? It is רבי מאיר, who says a person can transfer ownership of something that has not yet come into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing off the previous attempted proof. It says the source used for that proof follows only רבי מאיר, so it cannot settle the question for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a person can give rights in something that does not exist yet. So for him, a lien can also take hold of property the borrower will buy later. A ruling that fits רבי מאיר does not prove what the חכמים hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a different explanation
Whose view is this?
Transfers ownership
Something not yet in existence

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not ruling on liens directly here. The גמרא applies his general rule about transferring things that do not exist yet to property a borrower will buy in the future.

phrases.english: Rather, whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Meir,
who says: A person can transfer ownership of
something that has not yet come into the world.
phrases.notes: So for him, a lien can also take hold of property the borrower hasn't bought yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought just before this point.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole earlier proof, because its source may reflect only רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source follows רבי מאיר, who allows transferring something not yet in existence, so it does not show what the חכמים hold.

steps.title: New proof from the משנה on antedated and postdated שטרות
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב מנהר פקוד, in the name of רבינא, quotes the משנה: antedated loan documents are invalid and postdated ones are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב from נהר פקוד said in the name of רבינא: Come and hear. Loan documents dated too early are invalid, and loan documents dated too late are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new proof begins. Here the גמרא only quotes the source; the argument from it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An antedated שטר is invalid because it lets the lender seize land the borrower sold before the loan really happened. A postdated שטר is accepted as valid. The next step builds a question about דאיקני out of that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a proof
Loan documents
Antedated; dated earlier than the real loan
Postdated; dated later than the real loan
Invalid / valid

phrases.english: Rav Yaakov from Nehar Pekod said
in the name of Ravina: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: The source is the משנה in שביעית 10:5.

phrases.english: Loan documents that are antedated are invalid,
phrases.notes: The date is earlier than the real loan, so the lender could wrongly take land the borrower sold before he borrowed.

phrases.english: and those that are postdated are valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יַעֲקֹב מִנְּהַר פְּקוֹד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off, a new proof is brought.
steps.raayaObject: Whether property acquired after the loan (דאיקני) is liened even after it was sold or inherited.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שביעית on מוקדמין and מאוחרין.

steps.title: Why postdated שטרות prove that דאיקני is liened
steps.stepSummary: If later-acquired property were not liened, a postdated שטר should be invalid, because property bought between the loan and the written date would look liened.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think that when a borrower writes 'what I will acquire,' then buys property and sells it or leaves it to heirs, the property is not liened, why are postdated documents valid? That case is דאיקני!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the משנה proves the point. It argues that the validity of postdated שטרות shows that later-acquired property is liened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the borrower buys land after the real loan but before the date written in the שטר, and sells it afterward. The שטר makes that land look liened. If דאיקני were not liened, the lender could wrongly seize it, so the משנה should have ruled the שטר invalid. Since the משנה calls it valid, דאיקני must be liened.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind; if you think
'What I will acquire'; property bought after the loan
Left to his heirs
Is subject to the lien
Why?

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an accepted rule about document dates depends on the basic question of whether later-acquired property can be liened.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that with 'what I will acquire,' if he acquired and sold,
phrases.notes: The borrower wrote in the שטר that property he buys in the future will also be liened.

phrases.english: or with 'what I will acquire,' if he acquired and left it to heirs, it is not liened;
then why are postdated documents valid?
It is a case of 'what I will acquire'!
phrases.notes: Land bought between the real loan and the later written date counts as property acquired after the loan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the argument out of the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That דאיקני which was bought and then sold or inherited is liened.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that מאוחרין are valid.

steps.title: This proof is also pushed off: the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה about postdated שטרות follows רבי מאיר, so it does not prove the view of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this משנה? It is רבי מאיר, who says a person can transfer something that has not yet come into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבינא's proof with the same answer it gave in step 1. The words repeat because the same reply is now used against a new proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי מאיר holds that later-acquired property can be liened, postdated שטרות cause no problem for him. The משנה can follow his view, so it tells us nothing about the חכמים, who may disagree.
steps.whatToRemember: Two proofs that דאיקני is liened have now been pushed off, each by saying the source follows רבי מאיר, who allows transferring a דבר שלא בא לעולם.

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Meir,
who says: A person can transfer ownership of
something that has not yet come into the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 2 and 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה about מאוחרין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may follow רבי מאיר alone, so it does not show what the חכמים hold.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a field that was improved
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא, in the name of רבא, brings a ברייתא. A creditor takes a field from a buyer who had improved it. The buyer then collects the field's original value even from sold property, but the improvement only from unsold property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said in the name of רבא: Come and hear. How does the rule about the improvement of land work? A man sold a field to his friend, and the buyer improved it. Then the seller's creditor came and took the field away. When the buyer collects from the seller, he collects the original value even from sold, liened property. He collects the improvement only from unsold, free property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, to try to settle the question. This step only sets out the case; the actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case has three people: the seller (who owes money), the buyer, and the seller's creditor. The creditor takes the whole field from the buyer, improvement included. The buyer can collect the field's basic value even from property the seller later sold to others, but the improvement only from property the seller still has.

keyTerms.meaning: Improvement, the added value that develops in a field after it is bought
He took it away; a creditor seizing property from a buyer to collect a debt
The principal; here, the original value of the field
Liened property that has already been sold to others
Free property that the seller still owns

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said in the name of Rava:
Come and hear:
Regarding the improvement of land, how so?
Where one sold a field to his friend,
and he (the buyer) improved it,
and a creditor came and seized it,
when he (the buyer) collects from the seller,
he collects the principal from liened, sold property,
and the improvement from free, unsold property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from postdated שטרות was rejected, a new source is brought to settle the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That property acquired after the loan (דאקני) is liened, even according to the חכמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a creditor taking a field together with its improvement

steps.title: Why can the creditor take the improvement?
steps.stepSummary: The improvement did not exist when the loan was made. If later-acquired property is not liened, the creditor should not be able to take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think that when the borrower wrote 'what I will acquire' and then acquired and sold it, or acquired and left it to his heirs, it is not liened, then why does the creditor collect the improvement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof out of the ברייתא. The improvement came into being after the loan, yet the creditor still takes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The improvement is like property the borrower got after the loan, since it did not exist on the day of the loan. Taking it is only allowed if later-acquired property is liened. So the ברייתא seems to prove that דאקני is liened, even after it was sold or inherited.

keyTerms.meaning: "That I will acquire"; a clause liening property the borrower will get in the future
Is liened, held as security for the debt
And he left it to his heirs
If it enters your mind, if you think

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that with 'what I will acquire,' where he acquired and sold,
and with 'what I will acquire,' where he acquired and left it to heirs,
it is not liened,
why does the creditor collect the improvement?
phrases.notes: The improvement didn't exist when the loan was given, so it is like something acquired later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the ברייתא from step 5 proves that later-acquired property is liened.
steps.raayaObject: Later-acquired property (דאקני) is liened even after it was sold or inherited
steps.raayaSupportSource: The creditor's right to take the improvement, which did not exist at the time of the loan

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a person can transfer something that does not yet exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי מאיר, who says a person can transfer ownership of something that has not yet come into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by saying the ברייתא follows one particular תנא, רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that one can transfer or lien something that does not exist yet, so of course the improvement is liened. The question being asked is according to the חכמים, who disagree with him, so the ברייתא proves nothing for them. This is the same type of answer as in steps 1 and 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
Something that has not yet come into existence
Transfers ownership

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the הלכה follows רבי מאיר. The גמרא only says the ברייתא cannot prove what the חכמים hold.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Meir,
who says: A person can transfer ownership of
something that has not come into the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא about improvements
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר's view that one can transfer something not yet in existence, while the question is asked according to the חכמים.
steps.whatToRemember: Every proof here that later-acquired property is liened has been pushed off with the same answer: that source follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Two loans, then property acquired: which lender comes first?
steps.stepSummary: If later-acquired property is not liened, there is nothing more to ask. If it is liened, then where a person borrowed twice and later acquired property, does the first lender or the second lender have the lien?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that when he wrote 'what I will acquire' and acquired and sold it, or acquired and left it to heirs, it is not liened, then it is simply not liened. If you say it is liened: if he borrowed, and borrowed again, and then acquired property, what is the law? Is it liened to the first lender or to the last lender?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question that only comes up if later-acquired property is liened. It asks which of two earlier lenders has the claim on property bought after both loans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the earlier lender comes first, because his lien started earlier. Here, though, the property only came to the borrower after both loans, so both liens start on that property at the same moment. The question is whether the first lender still has priority, or whether the later lender does.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, if you conclude
He borrowed, and borrowed again from another lender
To the first one
To the last one

steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides the order of collection between creditors when the property came into the borrower's hands only after all the loans.

phrases.english: If you say:
with 'what I will acquire,' where he acquired and sold,
and with 'what I will acquire,' where he acquired and left it to heirs,
it is not liened,
then it is not liened, and there is nothing more to ask.
If you say it is liened,
if he borrowed and borrowed again, and then acquired property, what is the law?
Is it liened to the first lender, or is it liened to the last lender?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After failing to settle the first question, the גמרא asks a follow-up question that assumes later-acquired property is liened.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When property is acquired after two loans that both lien future property, does the first lender or the later lender have the lien on it?

steps.title: From ארץ ישראל: the first lender acquires
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reports that this exact question came up, and the answer sent from ארץ ישראל was that the first lender acquires the later property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: We asked this very question, and they sent back from there (ארץ ישראל): the first lender acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the question from Step 8. Based on a ruling from ארץ ישראל, the first lender gets the later-acquired property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the first lender's lien came first in time. So when the new property arrives, his earlier claim wins over the second lender.

keyTerms.meaning: We asked this question
They sent from there, meaning from the חכמים of ארץ ישראל
The first lender acquires

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
This matter was asked before us,
and they sent from there:
The first lender acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הָא מִילְּתָא אִיבַּעְיָא לַן, וּשְׁלַחוּ מִתָּם
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which lender has the lien on property acquired after both loans.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first lender acquires, because his lien came first.

steps.title: רב הונא and רבה בר אבוה: the lenders split it
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the two lenders split the later property, and רבה בר אבוה teaches the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: They split it. And רבה בר אבוה also teaches: They split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, opposing answer. The two lenders share the later-acquired property equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is that the property did not exist when either loan was made. The lien of both lenders takes hold at the same moment, when the property is acquired, so neither one comes first. רבה בר אבוה's teaching adds support to רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: They divide it between them
And so he teaches, meaning another source agrees

phrases.english: Rav Huna says: They divide it.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תָּנֵי רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: יַחְלוֹקוּ.
phrases.english: And so Rabba bar Avuh teaches: They divide it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to the one in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which lender has the lien on property acquired after both loans.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Neither lender has priority, so they split it.

steps.title: רב אשי's first and final rulings
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports that רב אשי first taught 'the first lender acquires,' but in his later round of teaching ruled 'they split it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: In רב אשי's first round of teaching, he told us: The first acquires. In רב אשי's last round, he told us: They split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב אשי himself changed his mind. He moved from the first view to the second view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי taught the גמרא in more than one round. His final round counts as his settled view, so the change supports 'they split it.' This sets up the הלכה in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The first round, or first edition, of teaching
The last round, or final edition, of teaching

phrases.english: Ravina said:
In the first round of Rav Ashi's teaching,
he told us: The first lender acquires.
In the last round of Rav Ashi's teaching,
he told us: They divide it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: מַהְדּוּרָא קַמָּא דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב אשי held each of the two views from Steps 9 and 10 at different times, ending with the second.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי's final position is that the lenders divide the property.

steps.title: The הלכה: the lenders split it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is that the two lenders divide the later-acquired property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: They split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling for the question from Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the two answers, the גמרא decides in favor of 'they split it.' The first lender does not get priority on property acquired after both loans.

keyTerms.meaning: And the practical law is

steps.whatToRemember: If someone borrowed from two lenders and later acquired property, both liens take hold at the same moment. So the lenders divide the property (יחלוקו).

phrases.english: And the halakha is: They divide it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two views from Steps 9 to 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The lenders divide later-acquired property between them.

steps.title: Challenge from the improved-field ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges 'they split it' using the ברייתא from Step 5. That ברייתא says the buyer collects the improvement, when it should say he collects only half of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: How does the rule work for improvement of land? Someone sold a field to his friend, and the buyer improved it. Then a creditor of the seller came and took it away. When the buyer collects from the seller, he collects the main value even from sold property, and the improvement only from unsold property. But if 'they split it' is true, it should say he collects half the improvement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the הלכה it just gave, 'they split it,' by quoting the ברייתא from Step 5 again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The improvement came into existence after both the creditor's loan and the sale. So the creditor and the buyer are like two lenders whose claims take hold at the same moment. If they split it, the creditor should take only half the improvement, and the buyer should need to collect only half of it from the seller. Yet the ברייתא speaks of collecting the whole improvement.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection from a תנאי source
Improvement, the added value of the land
The main value, the original price of the field
And if it is so, meaning if your ruling is correct

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא was used back in Step 5 to discuss whether later property is liened at all. Here the same ברייתא is used for a new purpose: to challenge 'they split it.'

phrases.english: They objected: For improvement of land, how so?
Where one sold a field to another, and he improved it,
phrases.notes: The buyer is the one who improved the field.

phrases.english: and a creditor came and took it away,
when he collects,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the buyer, collecting his loss back from the seller.

phrases.english: he collects the principal from sold property,
and the improvement from unsold property.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אִיתָא, חֲצִי שֶׁבַח מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: And if it is so, it should say half the improvement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הלכה from Step 12, using the ברייתא from Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הלכה that the lenders divide later-acquired property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The improvement came after both claims, so splitting would mean only half the improvement is involved. But the ברייתא speaks of collecting the whole improvement.

steps.title: 'Collects' means half the improvement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that when the ברייתא says the buyer 'collects' the improvement, it means he collects half of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'collects' mean in what the ברייתא teaches? Half the improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא's word 'collects' in a narrower way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never says 'all' of the improvement; it just says 'collects.' The גמרא reads that word as half the improvement, which fits 'they split it.' So the הלכה from Step 12 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: That it teaches, meaning what the ברייתא says

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling 'they split it' survives the challenge, because the ברייתא can be read as talking about half the improvement.

phrases.english: What is the 'collects' that it also teaches?
phrases.notes: The word 'collects' here refers to the improvement, the part being challenged.

phrases.english: Half of the improvement.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Collects' seemed to mean collecting the entire improvement.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Collects' means collecting half the improvement, which fits 'they split it.'
